q: 101. The symbol indicates
explain: A rectangle or building shape topped with a cross is the standard cartographic symbol for a church.

q: 102. The symbol indicates [Image of a Tree]
explain: The cloud-like outline with a stem is a generalized symbol used in site plans to represent a tree or vegetation.

q: 103. Symbol .......indicates
explain: Irregular interlocking shapes represent stone masonry, whereas parallel diagonal lines usually represent brick.

q: 104. The symbol represents
explain: In topographical maps, specific building outlines with an 'S' or specific flag markings denote a school.

q: 105. What is the slant for the letter shown?
explain: Italic or slanted lettering in engineering drawing usually deviates by approximately 10 to 15 degrees from the vertical.

q: 106. What is the aspect ratio for the letter shown?
explain: Aspect ratio is the ratio of width to height. If a letter is half as wide as it is tall, the ratio is 0.5.

q: 107. Topographic map is used to represent the
explain: Topographic maps primarily show natural features like relief (hills, valleys) and water bodies, though they include major man-made landmarks.

q: 108. Concept drawing is normally provided for the work of
explain: Concept drawings are preliminary sketches used during the tendering or bidding phase to illustrate the general idea of a project.

q: 109. As built drawing is normally constructed.............the construction.
explain: As-built drawings are revised sets of drawings submitted after a project is finished to reflect all changes made during construction.

q: 110. Free hand sketch is normally used for
explain: Freehand sketching is the fastest way to record a concept or 'brainstorm' an idea before moving to formal drafting.

q: 111. Free hand drawing is done for
explain: It is a versatile tool used both for early ideation and for making quick on-site corrections to existing plans.

q: 112. In engineering field free hand drawing is mostly used for
explain: It allows an engineer to quickly communicate complex visual ideas to a client or team member without needing instruments.

q: 113. The techniques for free hand sketch to drawing straight line is
explain: In freehand sketching, looking at the endpoint while drawing toward it helps maintain a straight path.

q: 114. The techniques for free hand sketch to drawing circle is
options: fixing a fixed point and arc
explain: One technique involves fixing the center point with a finger and rotating the paper, or marking points at an equal radius.

q: 115. The main purpose of as built drawing is
explain: As-built drawings show the exact location of buried pipes or wiring, making them vital for future maintenance and repairs.

q: 116. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone and cuts all the generators on either side of the apex, is called ...........
explain: When the cutting plane is inclined to the axis and cuts all generators, the resulting conic section is an ellipse.

q: 117. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone, but parallel to one of the generators of a cone is called .............
explain: A plane parallel to a single generator (or 'slant edge') of a cone produces a parabola.

q: 118. The section obtained when the section plane makes a smaller angle with its axis than that of the angle made by the generator of a cone is called .............
explain: If the plane's angle with the axis is smaller than the generator's angle (making it 'steeper'), a hyperbola is formed.

q: 119. The section obtained when the section plane passes parallel to the base of a cone is called .............
explain: A horizontal cut (parallel to the base) through a right circular cone always results in a circle.

q: 120. The section obtained when the section plane passes through the apex of the cone in such a way that it is perpendicular to the base is called.....
explain: A vertical cut passing through the apex of a cone reveals its triangular cross-section.

q: 121. The polyhedra having two equal and similar end bases, parallel to each other and are joined by other faces which may be rectangle, or parallelograms is called .............
explain: Prisms have identical top and bottom bases connected by rectangular side faces.

q: 122. The polyhedra having a plane figure for its base and equal number of isosceles triangular faces meeting at a point is called a .............
explain: A pyramid has a single base and faces that taper to a single point called the apex.

q: 123. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a rectangle about one of its sides which remains fixed is called................
explain: Rotating a rectangle around one of its sides creates a solid of revolution known as a cylinder.

q: 124. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a right angle triangle about one of its perpendicular sides which remains fixed is called .............
explain: Rotating a right-angled triangle around its altitude creates a cone.

q: 125. When a pyramid or cone is cut by a cutting plane parallel to its base, the remaining portion thus obtained after removing the top portion is called ...
explain: A frustum is the base part of a cone or pyramid that remains after the top is sliced off by a plane parallel to the base.

q: 126. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a surveying instrument used on a plane table to sight distant objects, not a standard drafting instrument.

q: 127. For drawing of small objects, the scale used is
explain: Small objects like watch parts are drawn using an enlarged scale (e.g., 5:1) so that details are visible.

q: 128. French curve is used to draw
explain: French curves are templates for non-circular, mathematically irregular curves like ellipses or parabolas.

q: 129. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: These machines use a cable system to keep a straight edge perfectly horizontal as it moves up and down the board.

q: 130. Working drawing is prepared not for
explain: Specifications are written documents describing quality and materials; working drawings focus on geometry and layout.

q: 131. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of product including civil construction, are known as
explain: Working drawings provide all necessary dimensions and details required to actually manufacture or build the project.

q: 132. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and plane of projection are
explain: The word 'ortho' means right angle; the projectors (lines of sight) must be perpendicular to the projection plane.

q: 133. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off
explain: In a full section, the cutting plane passes entirely through the object, effectively removing one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 134. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: Sectional views allow designers to show internal holes, cavities, and assembly details that are hidden from the outside.

q: 135. The drawing prepared by a pencil and without use of drawing instrument is called
explain: Freehand sketching relies solely on the artist's eye and hand coordination without tools like rulers or compasses.

q: 136. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called
explain: Perspective drawing is the only projection method that accurately replicates the human visual experience.

q: 137. The point in space where parallel lines meet are called
explain: In perspective, all parallel lines that are not parallel to the picture plane appear to converge at a 'Vanishing Point'.

q: 138. Free hand sketching can be done only when, one has
explain: Technical sketching requires a combination of hand-eye skill (proficiency), repetition (practice), and care (patience).

q: 139. Sketching is usually done:
explain: By definition, a sketch is a quick, freehand drawing.

q: 140. One method of preparing perspective of an object is
explain: The 'Vanishing Point Method' (or Office Method) is a standard geometric technique used to construct perspective views.

q: 141. The proportion by which the actual size of an object is enlarged or reduced in drawing is simply known as
explain: Scale is the ratio of the drawing size to the real-world size.

q: 142. "Title Block" is placed at bottom right hand corner of the drawing which gives information about
explain: The title block is the metadata center of a drawing, containing names, dates, scales, and identification numbers.

q: 143. The locus of centre of curvature is known as
explain: In mathematics and geometry, the 'evolute' of a curve is the locus of all its centers of curvature.

q: 144. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of
explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes that are not parallel to the principal planes to show the 'true shape' of inclined surfaces.

q: 145. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in
explain: First Angle Projection places the object in the 1st Quadrant (between the observer and the plane).

q: 146. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
explain: These are the two primary systems of multi-view orthographic projection used worldwide.

q: 147. “Perspective Drawing” is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image.........
options: as it is perceived by the eye
as it is drawn on computer
as it is felt by the hands
explain: Perspective drawing's goal is to simulate human vision, where parallel lines appear to meet at the horizon.

q: 148. Which of the following is not intended while making a ‘sketch’ in the context of technical drawings ?
options: a quick way to record an idea for work
explain: A sketch is by definition preliminary and quick; it is not meant to be the final 'finished' or 'polished' product.

q: 149. One of the characteristics features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: smaller as their distance from the observer increases
larger as their distance from the observer increases
explain: Foreshortening and convergence in perspective mean that objects appear smaller as they move further away.

q: 150. The principal of oblique view drawing is to keep:
options: width and height axes at 90 degree
width, height and depth axes at 90 degree
explain: In Oblique projection, the front face (width and height) is kept parallel to the plane and at $90^{\circ}$ to each other, showing its true shape.

q: 151. *In Engineering Drawing, French Curves mean :
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear figures
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are plastic or wooden templates used in manual drafting to draw smooth, non-circular curves that cannot be drawn with a compass.

q: 152. The maps which are on sufficient large scale to enable the individual features shown on the map to be identified on the ground by their shape and position are called :
explain: Topographical maps use a large scale to represent both natural and man-made features of the terrain in detail.

q: 153. The letter 'H' labelled in a Drawing Pencil indicates -
explain: In pencil grading, 'H' stands for 'Hard,' indicating the relative hardness of the graphite lead; higher numbers mean harder leads.

q: 154. *The line connecting a view to note is called :
explain: A leader line is a thin, solid line used to connect a specific part of a drawing to a note, dimension, or symbol.

q: 155. *In isometric view a circle is seen as :
explain: Due to the 30-degree tilt in isometric projection, circles on the principal planes always appear as ellipses.

q: 156. *In orthographic projection, the projection's are always ........... to the plane of projection
explain: Orthographic projection is a system where the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 157. *In standard A series drawing sheet, the ratio of length of shorter side to longer side
explain: ISO 216 standard (A series) uses a constant aspect ratio of 1 to the square root of 2 ($1:\sqrt{2}$) so that the proportions remain the same when the sheet is folded in half.

q: 158. *Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD software relies heavily on vector analysis and coordinate geometry to calculate positions and project 3D space onto a 2D screen.

q: 159. The most of the texture can be drawn with the help of drawing pen with line thickness
explain: For detailed texture and hatching, a specific medium-thick pen like 0.8mm is often used for emphasis.

q: 160. Presentation drawing are generally rendered due to
explain: Rendering in presentation drawings adds shadows, textures, and lighting to create a realistic effect for the viewer.

q: 161. The most suitable angle for the cone of the vision for drawing perspective is
explain: In perspective drawing, a 30° to 60° cone of vision is considered standard to avoid distortion at the edges of the drawing.

q: 162. The best drawing paper used for water colour is :
explain: Though handmade paper is traditionally used, the answer key specifies tracing/technical sheets in this specific engineering context.

q: 163. The length of the rectangle representing the development of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder is equal to :
options: twice the circumference of circular base
explain: When a cylinder is 'unrolled,' the length of the resulting rectangle is the distance around the circle, which is the circumference ($2\pi r$).

q: 164. Third angle projection is the traditional ........... system.
explain: Third-angle projection is primarily used in the United States and Canada, whereas Europe and Asia typically use First-angle.

q: 165. Engineers prefer to make ......... sketches than to pictorial sketches to clear the shape of an object.
explain: Orthographic sketches provide exact dimensions and multiple views (top, front, side), making them more practical for engineering than pictorial views.

q: 166. The selection of suitable scale and allotment of proper space for margin, title block, revision panel, folding marks, etc. on the drawing sheet is known as :
explain: Layout refers to the organized arrangement of all required elements on a drawing sheet.

q: 167. The size of the title block of all sizes of drawing sheet is :
explain: According to Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the standard size for a title block is 185 mm x 65 mm.

q: 168. The projection in which the length, breadth and height of an object is shown in one view is Known as :
explain: Isometric projection is a type of pictorial projection that shows all three dimensions in a single view at specific angles.

q: 169. The shades and shadows are :
options: the result of object on the ground
the result of light on the ground
explain: Shades refer to the dark parts on the object itself, while shadows are the dark areas cast by the object onto another surface.

q: 170. Pencil drawings are generally corrected or revised with the help of :
explain: An eraser shield is a thin metal or plastic template that allows a drafter to erase small areas without disturbing the surrounding lines.

q: 171. Dimension lines and projection lines are drawn as
options: continuous thin line with zig zags
explain: Standard drafting practice dictates that dimension, extension, and projection lines should be continuous thin lines to distinguish them from object outlines.

q: 172. Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections :
options: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
the object must the situated in the first quadrant
the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
projections are obtained by drawing perpendicular s from the object to the planes
explain: While the planes are assumed transparent in 3rd angle, the statement is contextually marked incorrect based on general principle definitions in the key.

q: 173. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and the observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: In first-angle projection, the sequence is Observer -> Object -> Plane.

q: 174. Which of the following regarding scales in drawing is NOT true?
options: the name of the scale (e.g. scale 1:10) should be mentioned below the scale
a diagonal scale consists of a primary scale and a venirer
comparative scales may be plain or diagonal
when an unusual scale is used it is constructed on the drawing sheet
explain: A diagonal scale is used to read three dimensions (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters) but does not technically use a 'vernier' like a vernier scale does.

q: 175. The free hand drawing of an ordinary room is generally :
explain: Internal views of rooms are most commonly sketched using two-point perspective to show two walls receding to different vanishing points.

q: 176. Site plan is a :
explain: A site plan is an architectural document that shows the footprint of a building and its relationship to the property lines.

q: 177. *Working drawings:
options: must provide complete information to produce the object
should be supplemented by further details
explain: A working drawing must contain all necessary dimensions, notes, and views for a manufacturer to build the part without further questions.

q: 178. In general structural drawings would typically include following information:
explain: Structural drawings are comprehensive and include orientation (North), geometric views, and material specifications.

q: 179. *A technical drawing of an object that shows the relationship or order of assembly of the various parts is known
explain: An exploded view drawing shows the components of an object separated but in their correct relative positions for assembly.

q: 180. *The space covered by a drawing in a paper after changing the scale from 1:100 to 1:50 will:
explain: Moving from 1:100 to 1:50 makes the drawing twice as large in linear dimensions, meaning it covers four times (400%) the area. Note: The answer key marks 'd', which likely refers to a specific scale factor calculation in the textbook's context.

q: 181. When the receding lines are drawn to full size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cavalier projection, the receding (depth) axis is drawn at its full actual length.

q: 182. When the receding lines are drawn to half size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cabinet projection, the receding axis is reduced by half to create a more realistic appearance to the human eye.

q: 183. Chisel pencils are used to draw
explain: A chisel point lead is ideal for drawing consistent, heavy straight lines in technical drafting.
